title: Distinguish quotient objects from their representatives
obstacle: A statement about equivalence classes is being used as a statement about chosen representatives.
procedure: Identify which statements concern classes and which concern representatives.
Prove invariance before descending a construction, or supply the additional hypotheses needed to choose and compare representatives.
Keep class equality and representative equality as separate typed claims.
verification: Lean-check the descended construction or representative bridge with all invariance or uniqueness hypotheses explicit.
positive_example: Descend a function after proving it has equal values on equivalent inputs.
negative_example: Evaluate an arbitrary representative-dependent function on a quotient class.

evidence.note: Editorially generalized guidance under this maintenance policy; no independent effectiveness result or proof acceptance is claimed.
